attacks.claim: The day card hardcodes a white background, so under dark mode (~30% of users) the card stays white while the page, text and muted colors switch to dark palette. Light text (#f2f2f7) on white cards is unreadable and the meta text (#a1a1a6) on white has very poor contrast.
The Figma/QA was only run in light mode (Chrome 1440px light, iPhone 14 light), so the dark-mode regression above was never caught despite dark mode being a supported, large user segment.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass

attacks.claim: Dark-mode text contrast fails WCAG on the white day cards; the QA claims accessibility 100 only for the light theme, so the score does not cover the shipped dark experience.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: contrast verification in dark mode; .day-card background #ffffff with color var(--text) resolving to #f2f2f7 in dark mode

attacks.claim: The mobile sticky action bar is position:fixed with a 72px height but the page has no bottom padding on .planner, so the last day card (Sunday, last child of .planner) can be hidden behind the bar when scrolled to the end.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } and "Sunday is the last child of .planner" with .planner { padding: 16px; ... }

attacks.claim: The removal of the tile-level '+ List' button turns adding a recipe's ingredients to the list into a 6-step flow, while the brief says this is the most frequent planner action (9.4x/week per WAU) and 64% of it happens on mobile. This is a large friction regression on the primary task.
attacks.evidence: tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo"; The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed

attacks.claim: The redesign optimizes for declutter while removing the most-used action, and the brief's usage data argues against it. Nothing in the artifact shows the tradeoff was tested with users.
attacks.evidence: Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week ...); ABSENT: user testing or A/B evidence that the removal improves outcomes

attacks.claim: Rollback is via a feature flag with no data migration, which is good, but the flag is not described as covering the new action-bar or any shared CSS, so a partial rollback could leave mixed styles. Observability lists only JS errors, WAU and bounce, with no alert on shopping-list addition drop.
attacks.evidence: Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.

attacks.claim: The 'Generate shopping list' action adds all planned recipes for the week in one tap with no stated confirmation, idempotency or rate limit, so repeated taps could duplicate ingredients.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)

attacks.claim: Decorative recipe images use alt="" which is acceptable only if the title is present; this is fine, but the drag-and-drop move is only exposed via overflow menu for keyboard users, and the Swap/overflow buttons are small on mobile with no stated target size check.
attacks.evidence: and

attacks.claim: The Lighthouse and QA results are for light mode and desktop/one iPhone; no mobile 360px Android test is listed despite the brief's 360-414px mobile majority.
attacks.evidence: Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass; Lighthouse mobile: performance 91

attacks.claim: Shipping to 100% of users at once with no staged rollout limits the blast radius of the dark-mode and friction regressions above.
